_note: Values that encode a DECISION rather than a measurement. tools/check_decisions.py recomputes each from its real source and REFUSES if one has moved, because a decision changing is exactly the case where a deliberate act should be required — and editing this file in the same commit is that act. Most numbers in this build move every run; these do not. See own error 48.

siteOrigin.why: Where this archive lives, stated in three files that must agree: astro.config.mjs's `site`, site/public/CNAME and site/public/robots.txt's Sitemap line. MOVED 12 OCTOBER 2026 from daviddef.github.io/TheDArcy, because defranceski.com is a Pages site served by its own repo and project paths do not inherit it — defranceski.com/TheDArcy/ returns 404 — so a subdomain was the only route. THE CHECK EXISTS BECAUSE THE MOVE LEFT ONE OF THE THREE BEHIND. robots.txt went on naming a sitemap at the old origin while everything else had moved; the build was green and every gate passed, because no gate read it. A reader would never notice and a crawler reads nothing else. CNAME is the dangerous one: this repo deploys by Actions uploading site/dist, and a deploy carrying no CNAME DETACHES the custom domain, so a wrong or missing one takes the whole archive dark rather than leaving a stale line. The gate does not judge whether the address is right — nobody here can — only whether the three agree, and all three failure modes were provoked and seen to refuse before it was trusted.

livingPolicy.why: named-place: a living person is named, with their relationships and their town and country, and nothing more. MOVED 16 OCTOBER 2026 from named-bare-by-omission (no living person published as a person at all) on David's ruling, and the same day to version 2 of the standard (see livingRule): who is living is decided by the kit's one definition, and every person the archive names has a page. The key is present in living.json and people.js falls back to the same string.

namedLiving.why: The six living people named on purpose in prose, confirmed deliberately by David (14 and 15 September 2026). Anyone appearing or disappearing here is a change to who this archive names on purpose. They are unchanged by the 16 October 2026 standard; every other living person is now named too, and that is the policy above, not this list.

grafts.why: The two rejected links and how many people hang off each. /how-far-back publishes these counts in a sentence — 71 on a single unevidenced link, 27 on a disproved one — so if the tree moves, that sentence goes stale.

retiredAllow.why: The pages allowed to restate a withdrawn reading, because their subject IS the withdrawal. Widening this list quietly would disarm the retired-reading gate.

livingExemptions.why: Every phrase the living gate is told to let through — the union of living.json's `named`, `namesakes` and `allow`. namedLiving watches who this archive decided to publish; this watches the whole exemption surface, because a phrase added to namesakes is exempted just as effectively and nothing else here would say so.

heldOutIds.why: David's ruling of 16 October 2026: the living woman whose DNA result the archive describes is HELD OUT. She has no page, no record, no name as anybody's relative, and nothing in a file the site serves or the repository tracks that could be traced to her. /dna/ says she is not named, and that sentence has to stay true. Held by id only; no file, message or log names her. tools/check_living_standard.py proves the id is absent from every data file and built page; tools/check_living.py, which reads the tree, proves her name is too.

value.dna-tester: held by id; a person whose DNA result the archive describes without naming her
value.possible-minor: an undated person with a living parent, not recorded dead and with no public source; a child with a known birth year is NOT held out

heldOutRules.why: David's ruling of 16 October 2026, version 2, amended the same day: a person who might be a child is HELD OUT only when nothing says how old they are. The test is the kit's (living_rule.possible_minor): not recorded dead, no public source, no birth year, and a living parent. A child with a KNOWN birth year under 18 is not held out: they are named with their relationships and their town and country, have a page and are noindex, like any living person. A rule, not a list of names: tools/gedcom.held_out() decides it from the tree, tools/build_site_data.py and tools/ancestry.py both use it, and tools/check_living.py recomputes it independently with its own facts and proves not one of them has a page, a record, or a name as anybody's relative. The count met and left out is written to living.json, never their names.

recordedDeadKinds.why: David's ruling of 16 October 2026: a person the tree RECORDS as deceased is dead whether or not a date exists. MyHeritage writes a death event with no date for somebody it knows to be dead and does not know when; a burial says the same. They are ordinary dead people: indexable pages, and no date or field they do not already hold in the tree. Under version 2 the 100-year inference through the family graph is gone altogether: a person with no birth year is not living.

livingRule.why: David's ruling of 16 October 2026, version 2, written once for every archive in the kit's living_rule.py and kit/data/public-sources.json: living is 80 or younger by year (this year minus the birth year) with no death or burial recorded and no public source; a person with no birth year is not living; an undated person with a living parent (who might be a child) is held out, and a child with a KNOWN birth year is not (David, 16 October 2026): every child follows the standard. The numbers and the list of public record sources belong to the whole estate, so a kit move that changes one changes who is living here without a line of this repository changing. This watches them: a re-pin that moves one is refused until the move is recorded here, in the same commit. Declared again 16 October 2026 with kit 27af004: user-built trees that MyHeritage files under research (Geni World Family Tree, WikiTree, Filae, GenealogieOnline) are excluded from the public sources, being private-tree entries, not records. MOVED 17 OCTOBER 2026 with the kit pin to 2d5275a, which adds MATRICULA (the online parish registers) to the public record sources, so a citation to it now means a person is not living. MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: no person in this archive's tree cites Matricula, so the addition changes nobody's status here; the living gate's counts are unchanged at 39 living pages and 544 living in the tree.

samePerson.why: Tree people declared to be ONE person entered twice, by tree id as copy->primary, ruled 16 October 2026 on David's word as relayed by the landing-site session after an audit of this archive's pages. Eight pairs: the two copies of Joseph Samuel Sneyd, his six children who exist twice (one under each copy of him), and Ralph Sneyd born 1863. A copy KEEPS ITS ADDRESS and says it is the same person, carries a canonical link to the primary, and is left out of the sitemap and the search index; the primary is untouched. NOT declared on purpose: the two Ralph Sneyds of 1793 have different parents and are a Keele conflation, not a duplicate (work list 151), and no pair the audit rated low, because a shared parent and nothing else is how a family reuses a name. The primary is the copy that draws more of the family, then the one that cites more, and that rule is written in same-person.json beside each choice so it can be audited.
